working_interpretation: Information gained before the fight helps determine and conceal the final setup.
A first move can spend resources without entering effective reach; voluntary retreat preserves a later move.
Pressure on one group can invite pursuit while a second group gains a different option.
Whether a backline lives a dive depends on whether the attack was allowed to stage well.
The first-moving side can decline the obvious chase or stack another advantage; bait may fail.
An opening for the frontline need not be an all-team turn.
Ult counts alone omit the fight result, point position, subsequent setup, and charge gained.
Economy and cooldown-cycle importance vary with composition and matchup.
A tank's entry matters partly through what damage players can do during its brief window.
Excessive safety removes pressure; excessive reach makes the damage dealer an easy trade.
Knowing the right explanation after a fight differs from seeing and executing it during play.
Hero-balance opinions and pre-release predictions are not evidence that a matchup actually works.
